Subject: Request: Circuit-breaker canary thresholds & pinning — SLA exception for Finex rollout

Chris / Maya —

Thanks again for the sync today. As discussed, Finex wants a gradual model swap for their payments risk module with a 7-day canary before full cutover. The canary will briefly allow higher p95 latency during cold-cache windows while we validate accuracy at scale.

We need an SLA carve-out for the canary window that permits transient p95 spikes up to 1200ms for segments of traffic (up to 10% traffic slice), provided the following automatic mitigations are in place:

- Circuit-breaker: automatic rollback to the pinned previous model variant if error rate > 2% or p95 > 1200ms sustained for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Pinning: the previous version remains pinned as an immediate fallback; no traffic will be routed to a new variant if health checks fail.
- Observability: token-level traces and per-route latency/err-rate dashboards shared with Finex in real-time.

Attached: canary-health-config.yaml (thresholds + alert rules) and a draft SLA exception request docx for legal. We request approval for the exception and confirmation that Finex will accept a temporary exclusion from SLA credits while the canary is active.

Action requested: please confirm by EOD Mon (27 Jul) or let us know what minimum additional telemetry or contract language you need.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Appreciate the note and the config. A few clarifying Qs before I sign off with procurement:

1) Window semantics: when you say "sustained for 2 consecutive minutes" — does that mean two 1-minute aggregated buckets, or sliding-window 120s? We need the exact definition for our telemetry.
2) What happens to in-flight requests when the circuit-breaker trips? Do we cancel or finish them on the old variant?
3) If the canary is allowed to exceed p95 for up to 1200ms, will that be reported as a customer-visible incident or as an expected behaviour in the weekly report?

Also send me the expected cost delta for the canary phase (additional GPU ops / bandwidth). Procurement will want a number to justify the SLA carve-out.

If we get these answers quickly we can sign the exception and proceed with the 7-day plan.

—Chris

Chris / Vanessa —

Responding to the technical items:

1) Window definition: we will use a sliding 120s window evaluated every 30s for p95 and error-rate heuristics. That ensures short blips don't flip the breaker.

2) In-flight requests: the circuit-breaker initiates a soft-failover. New requests are routed to the pinned variant immediately; in-flight requests on the failing variant are allowed to finish (bounded by a 10s drain) to avoid partial responses. We mark them with a header X-Redwood-Fallback:true when we route to pinned.

3) Reporting: any trip will generate an immediate incident notification (Ops channel) and be annotated in the weekly latency/availability report as part of the canary exclusion window — per the SLA exception draft. It will not be treated as an SLA breach provided the mitigation behaved per spec.

Cost delta: approximate incremental GPU hours ~ 18 GPU-hours over 7 days due to duplicate traces and overlap; estimate ~$1,200 in incremental compute for the canary. I'll attach detailed stamping to the Drive link.

I've updated the canary-health-config.yaml in Drive to reflect the sliding-window semantics and drain timeout. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0B-Canary-Configs/finex-canary
